from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Disease dynamics track how viruses spread through populations.",
            "Mathematical models help predict outbreak outcomes.",
            "Consider 100 students: how many will get sick?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Why Models Matter", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show text 'Epidemics reshape history.' in #FFFFFF.
        epidemics_text = Text("Epidemics reshape history.", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(epidemics_text, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(epidemics_text))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display a growing timeline graphic in #00FF00.
        timeline = VGroup(
            Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D6"], color="#00FF00"),
            *[Dot(self.grid[f"D{i}"], color="#00FF00") for i in range(2, 7)]
        )
        self.play(Create(timeline))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in 'Models predict outcomes.' in #FFFF00.
        model_text = Text("Models predict outcomes.", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(model_text, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(model_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The population is split into three compartments.",
            "Susceptible, Infectious, and Recovered states.",
            "The model tracks transitions between these states."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Components: The S-I-R Framework", lecture_lines)

        # Assets
        s_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        s_text = Tex("S", color=WHITE).move_to(s_node.get_center())
        s_group = VGroup(s_node, s_text)

        i_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.5)
        i_text = Tex("I", color=WHITE).move_to(i_node.get_center())
        i_group = VGroup(i_node, i_text)

        r_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        r_text = Tex("R", color=WHITE).move_to(r_node.get_center())
        r_group = VGroup(r_node, r_text)

        flow_arrow_si = Arrow(s_group.get_right(), i_group.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        flow_arrow_ir = Arrow(i_group.get_right(), r_group.get_left(), color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(s_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(i_group, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(r_group, 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(s_group, i_group, r_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(Create(flow_arrow_si), Create(flow_arrow_ir))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(Indicate(flow_arrow_si, color="#FF9900"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Engine of Change: Differential Equations", [
            "Infection and recovery drive the dynamics.",
            "S to I, then I to R.",
            "The model visualizes these curves over time."
        ])

        # Formula components
        dS_dt = MathTex(r"\frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta S I", font_size=40)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(dS_dt, "C3")))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        beta_term = dS_dt[0][6:] # targets -\beta S I
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(Indicate(beta_term, color="#FF0000"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        bar = Rectangle(height=2, width=0.5, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(bar, "D4")
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(bar))
        self.play(bar.animate.set_height(0.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Threshold of Chaos: Understanding R0", [
            "- The Basic Reproduction Number, R0, defines growth.",
            "- If R0 exceeds one, the epidemic grows.",
            "- If R0 is below one, it disappears."
        ])
        
        formula = MathTex(r"R_0 = \frac{\beta}{\gamma}", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        r0_gt_1 = Text("R0 > 1", font_size=36, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(r0_gt_1, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        r0_lt_1 = Text("R0 < 1", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(r0_lt_1, 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(r0_gt_1, color=RED))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(r0_lt_1, color=GREEN))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Models help simulate intervention strategies.", "Social distancing can flatten the curve.", "Models inform vital public health decisions."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Summarize SIR model power
        text1 = Text("SIR Model Power:", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        desc1 = Text("Predicts epidemic trajectory", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        group1 = VGroup(text1, desc1).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(group1, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(group1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Social distancing: flatten the curve
        text2 = Text("Applications:", font_size=32, color="#FFFF00")
        list2 = Text("Pandemics, Networks", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        group2 = VGroup(text2, list2).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(group2, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(group2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Models inform decisions
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        final_call = Text("Make Informed Decisions!", font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(final_call, "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(final_call))
        self.wait(4)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(group1), FadeOut(group2), FadeOut(final_call))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: An Introduction to SIR Modeling

sections.title: The Hook: Why Models Matter
sections.content: Introduce the concept of infectious disease dynamics. Define the objective: using mathematics to predict how quickly a virus spreads through a population.
sections.example: Imagine a flu outbreak in a school of 100 students. How do we predict if 10 or 90 will get sick?

sections.title: Defining the Components: The S-I-R Framework
sections.content: Break down the population into three compartments: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered/Removed (R). Emphasize that these states are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.
sections.example: Visualize a colored marble analogy: Blue (S), Red (I), and Green (R). An I-marble 'bumps' into an S-marble, turning it Red.

sections.title: The Engine of Change: Differential Equations
sections.content: Explain the transition rates: S to I (infection rate) and I to R (recovery rate). Introduce the visual flow: S -> I -> R, noting that I drives the flux of S into R.
sections.example: Graph visualization showing an S-curve declining, an I-curve spiking (the 'hump'), and an R-curve climbing steadily.

sections.title: The Threshold of Chaos: Understanding R0
sections.content: Explain the Basic Reproduction Number (R0). If R0 > 1, the epidemic grows; if R0 < 1, it dies out. Connect this to the balance of infection and recovery rates.
sections.example: Compare two scenarios: a 'highly contagious' virus (one person infects 5) vs. a 'slower' virus (one person infects 0.8).

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Synthesize how the SIR model allows us to simulate interventions like social distancing or vaccination. Final takeaway: Models are lenses that help us make informed decisions.
sections.example: Show a simulation where 'social distancing' reduces the peak of the I-curve, preventing the healthcare system from being overwhelmed.
